title: Using Gemini API as a gameplay feature
author: venus_uni_dev

comments.author: Redditry199

replies.author: venus_uni_dev
replies.body:
Hey Redditry thanks for checking it out! I'd recommend downgrading the model to 3.5/3.6 on the free tier key and trying again.  
I also have a small budget for keys for testers, if you try it out for a while and run into rate limits send me an email at the contact listed on the page and I'd be happy to provide a paid key with a spend cap on it

replies.author: PaperDevGames
replies.body: My guy, why not Gemma 4? Locally? Or built in? Just a thought. It's an extra 2GB to 4GB or so for people who don't know/want to try the online API? Just a thought again...

replies.author: venus_uni_dev
replies.body:
Hey PaperDev! I actually did initially experiment with a local instance of Ollama running Qwen for classifying player actions (in my testing, local LLMs write very bad prose), but dropped it for a few reasons. One was that it added setup complexity and like you said a model download. The main reason though was that it was both slower and lower quality than Gemini, so I ended up switching.

I did a lot of AI roleplaying in my time with local models but frontier APIs have vastly exceeded the capabilities of what can run on my 4080. But you are right that asking people to put in their Gemini key is an undesirable point of friction... hopefully the increased quality is worth it
